output.brief: The remote promotion gap is mostly explained by eligibility, not by where people work. Remote staff are much less likely to have the 18 months in level needed to be nominated (32% eligible vs 74% office). Among eligible employees, the rates are nearly the same: 21.1% office versus 20.0% remote. Nomination rates (28.6% vs 28.2%) and committee approval of nominees (74% vs 71%) are also close. Job-family mix does not explain it either, since the mix is similar across arrangements. So the data does not support proximity bias as the main driver. Confidence is moderate. The remote comparison rests on 110 eligible people, and a small real gap cannot be ruled out. I did not check stretch-assignment access or attrition, so those remain open. Next steps: do not announce the three-day office rule, since it would penalise remote staff for a tenure artifact. Change promotion reporting to compare eligible staff only. Check whether remote staff are being given stretch work, and look at why remote staff have shorter time in level, such as recent hiring.
